threads.body: [General] This advice can overwrite an SRV target captured by the 3.7/4.0 module. `mongo-3.1` remains enabled on newer `mongo-java-driver` versions because `MongoClientOptions` is still present, and all of these modules instrument the same `BaseCluster` constructor. Thus the final cache value depends on advice ordering; if this seed-only advice runs last, an SRV client is reported as the driver's placeholder seed instead of its SRV host. Make this advice SRV-aware as well, or restrict this type instrumentation to driver versions where the newer cluster advice is not active.

replies.body:
Addressed in 43471ce5cfb3b44221a457610db88d2f45dbac14.

Analysis: The mongo-3.1 advice can run alongside the 3.7 and 4.0 advice on newer drivers. It must use the shared reflective SRV lookup before falling back to seeds so every active advice registers the same configured target.

Upsides: SRV clients retain their configured SRV host regardless of Byte Buddy advice order. The reflective helper keeps the advice compatible with drivers that predate ClusterSettings.getSrvHost().

Downsides: The legacy advice performs one cached reflective method invocation when the driver exposes getSrvHost().

threads.body: [General] Duplicate Unix-socket seeds are omitted even though this method deduplicates endpoints. The loop collapses duplicates into `hosts`, but this check uses the original list size, so two identical socket entries return `null` instead of the single logical socket target. Check the deduplicated endpoint count instead (and add the duplicate-socket case alongside `duplicateSeedsAreRemoved`).

replies.body:
Addressed in d9d09e3897a71ab3a388456dfb112e0cd1b2c398.

Analysis: MongoServerTarget deduplicates seed endpoints into hosts before building a target. The Unix-socket branch checked seeds.size(), so repeated copies of the same socket were treated as several logical endpoints and suppressed. Checking hosts.size() applies the same deduplication semantics to Unix sockets.

Upsides: Repeated copies of one Unix socket now produce one logical target, while distinct sockets and mixed socket and TCP endpoints remain suppressed.

Downsides: No material downside identified.
